need: choose the board for a new tower workstation
clues: the build needs two full-length graphics cards side by side
the user wants four memory modules installed
the full-size tower case takes boards 12 by 9.6 inches
the build also needs a sound card and a capture card
appliesWhen: a full-size tower needs the most memory and expansion slots
explanation: Full-size ATX boards measure 12 × 9.6 inches and usually have four DIMM slots and two or more x16 slots. That room makes ATX the choice for a tower with many cards and memory modules.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

need: choose the board for a compact office desktop
clues: the slim case takes boards up to 9.6 inches square but not 12-inch boards
the user needs a graphics card and a second card in the small case
two memory modules are all the user will ever need
the board must also fit a standard ATX case later if needed
appliesWhen: a smaller square board with a few expansion slots is enough
explanation: microATX boards are up to 9.6 × 9.6 inches, use the same power connectors as ATX, and fit in ATX cases. They trade some DIMM and expansion slots for a smaller size, but still have more than one slot.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

need: choose the board for a tiny home theater PC under a TV
clues: two memory modules will be plenty
only one expansion card will ever be installed
the small PC must stay quiet and use little power
the case takes boards no larger than 170 mm on each side
appliesWhen: the PC must be as small as possible and needs at most one expansion card
explanation: Mini-ITX boards are 6.7 × 6.7 inches (170 mm) with normally one PCIe slot. They are made for small, low-power systems such as home theater PCs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

need: choose the board for a rack server that runs large simulations
clues: the simulations already keep every core of a single processor busy
the server must hold two Xeon CPUs at the same time
the workload needs more memory slots and PCIe lanes than one processor gives
appliesWhen: the workload needs two or more physical CPUs in one system
explanation: A multisocket board holds two or more CPUs, which adds processing power, memory slots, and PCIe lanes. It is used in high-end servers and workstations for parallel work.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

need: choose the processor for a fanless handheld device that runs all day
clues: the battery must stay small to keep the device light
the device must stay cool in the user's hand
the software is built for mobile chips like those in phones
the case is sealed against dust and rain
appliesWhen: the device is mobile and must run cool on little power
explanation: ARM processors use a reduced instruction set, so they run cooler and use less power than x86-64 CPUs. That is why phones, tablets, and other mobile devices use them.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

need: choose the processor for a desktop that will have 32 GB of RAM
clues: a 32-bit processor could use only about 4 GB of that memory
the user still runs some old 32-bit Windows programs
the desktop runs standard Windows software built for Intel and AMD PCs
appliesWhen: the PC runs standard 64-bit desktop software and needs more than 4 GB of RAM
explanation: Older 32-bit x86 CPUs can address only 4 GB of RAM, while x86-64 CPUs support far more. x86-64 CPUs also run 32-bit software, so old programs still work.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

need: speed up video encoding on an editor's PC
clues: the encoding software splits its work across every thread it finds
the Task Manager graph shows all logical processors at full load during each render
the Device Manager list shows only four logical processors
the clock rate is already high but renders are still slow

answer.item: A CPU with more cores and threads

appliesWhen: the software spreads its work across many threads at once
explanation: Multicore CPUs have several physical cores in one package, and multithreading lets each core run two threads. Software that splits work into threads runs faster when more cores and threads are available.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

need: choose the processor for low-cost office PCs with no graphics card
clues: the small cases have no free expansion slot
the monitor will plug into the video port on the board's rear panel
users only run email, a browser, and spreadsheets

answer.item: A CPU with an integrated GPU

appliesWhen: the PC has no video card and its display connects to the board's own video port
explanation: Many Intel and AMD CPUs include a graphics unit; AMD calls these APUs. With a compatible board, the monitor plugs into the board's video port and no video card is needed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

need: install Windows on a new PC from a USB flash drive
clues: the flash drive starts Windows Setup on another PC
the PC keeps trying the blank SSD first and reports no operating system
the firmware has to start the installer before anything on the SSD
appliesWhen: the PC must start from a different device than it tries first
explanation: The boot order sets which device the firmware starts from. Put the flash drive first for the install, then set the system drive first again.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

need: stop anyone from using flash drives on the high-security PCs
clues: a flash drive found in the parking lot infected a PC last month
staff charge their phones from these PCs over cables that can also move files
the keyboards and mice on these PCs are PS/2
appliesWhen: the ports themselves must be turned off so no flash drive can be used
explanation: The firmware can turn USB ports off or block starting from USB. That stops USB drop attacks, where an infected flash drive is left for someone to plug in.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

need: stop rootkits from loading before Windows starts
clues: a rootkit replaced the startup loader on another company PC
the firmware must load only startup files signed by a trusted vendor
the PCs have UEFI firmware and run Windows 11
appliesWhen: the firmware must check the signature of every startup file
explanation: Secure Boot lets UEFI firmware check the digital signature of the boot loader and other boot files. Files that are not signed or were tampered with do not load, which blocks many rootkits.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

need: stop students from changing firmware settings on the lab PCs
clues: students have been changing the startup device order
the lab PCs must still start Windows after a power cut with no prompt
students already sign in to Windows with their own accounts
appliesWhen: only the setup utility must be locked while the PC still starts on its own
explanation: The administrator or supervisor password is asked for only when someone opens the firmware setup. The PC still starts the operating system normally, so it suits public PCs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

need: make sure no one but the owner can start a sensitive laptop at all
clues: the laptop holds client legal files and travels often
a prompt must appear right after power-on, before anything loads
the owner accepts typing a second secret at every start
appliesWhen: a secret must be entered before the PC starts any operating system
explanation: The boot or user password is asked for before the firmware starts any operating system. It means users must know a second password, so most organizations use it only where it is needed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

need: turn on BitLocker drive encryption on the office desktops
clues: the BitLocker setup says a required security chip was not found
the board has a built-in cryptoprocessor that is turned off in the firmware
the Windows 11 upgrade check also fails on these PCs

answer.item: Enable the TPM in the BIOS/UEFI

appliesWhen: the board already has a cryptoprocessor chip that only needs to be turned on
explanation: The Trusted Platform Module is a chip on the board that stores encryption keys. BitLocker and Windows 11 need TPM 2.0, and on many boards it must be turned on in the firmware first.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

need: add hardware key storage to an older server that has no TPM
clues: the auditors require keys that never leave dedicated hardware
the keys must live in a removable device with its own crypto chip
the server must create and manage many encryption keys quickly
appliesWhen: the system has no TPM chip, or many keys must be made and managed in a separate device
explanation: An HSM is a separate device, such as a PCIe card or USB unit, with its own cryptoprocessor that creates, stores, and manages keys. It gives TPM-like protection to a system that has no TPM and can serve many keys fast.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

need: run virtual machines on a developer's desktop
clues: the hypervisor install stops with a message that a CPU extension is turned off
the processor's spec sheet lists hardware virtualization support
the Hyper-V manager cannot start any guest machine

answer.item: Intel VT-x or AMD-V (SVM) in the BIOS/UEFI

appliesWhen: a hypervisor needs the CPU's hardware extension for guest machines
explanation: Hypervisors need the CPU's hardware virtualization extension, which is often turned off by default. Turn on Intel VT-x, or AMD-V (often labeled SVM), in the firmware's CPU menu.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

need: make an editing PC quiet while it is idle
clues: the case fans run at full speed even when the PC does nothing
all fans are plugged into the board's own 4-pin headers
the user wants the fans to speed up only under heavy load

answer.item: The fan speed settings in the BIOS/UEFI

appliesWhen: fans on the board's headers run at the wrong speed for the load
explanation: The firmware can set fan speeds or profiles such as quiet or optimal for fans connected to the board's headers. A 4-pin fan lets the board control its speed with PWM.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

need: make a PC in a hot storeroom warn the user before it overheats
clues: the case vents face a wall only a few centimeters away
the PC shut down without any warning twice last summer
the board has sensors for the CPU and chipset

answer.item: Temperature monitoring with a warning and shutdown limit

appliesWhen: the PC must react on its own when a sensor passes a set heat limit
explanation: Board sensors report the temperature of the CPU, GPU, and chipset. In the firmware you can set a maximum temperature that warns the user, shuts the PC down, or both.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

need: record music in a home studio with clean audio
clues: the built-in audio adds hiss to every recording
the producer needs a higher sampling rate and signal-to-noise ratio
the setup needs extra inputs and 7.1 surround outputs
appliesWhen: the built-in audio is not good enough for audio work
explanation: Built-in audio is fine for most users, but audio editors need a card with a higher sampling rate and signal-to-noise ratio. A good add-on card also gives more inputs and outputs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

need: run 3D design software and games smoothly
clues: the processor's built-in graphics stutters in 3D scenes
the 3D software lists a minimum amount of dedicated graphics memory
the user wants to drive two high-refresh monitors
appliesWhen: the display output itself must be faster than built-in graphics can make it
explanation: A video card creates the image sent to the monitors and has its own GPU and memory. It goes in a PCIe x16 slot and is much faster than built-in graphics for 3D work.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

need: save a game console's gameplay as files on a PC for editing
clues: the console has only an HDMI output
the streamer wants to show live console play in streaming software
the PC already has a good graphics card for its own monitor
appliesWhen: a signal from another device must be brought into the PC and recorded
explanation: A capture card takes a video signal from another source, such as a console or camera, and turns it into data the PC can record or stream. It does the opposite of a video card, which sends images out.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

need: add more wired connections to a Linux file server
clues: the server has only one built-in RJ-45 port
two links must be bonded for more bandwidth
the server must stay online if one cable fails

answer.item: A network interface card with more ports

appliesWhen: the computer needs more or faster wired Ethernet connections
explanation: An add-on NIC gives one or more extra RJ-45 ports. The ports can be teamed for link aggregation or redundancy.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies

need: connect an external SATA drive enclosure to a desktop
clues: the enclosure has no USB port
the desktop has no such port on its rear panel
a free PCIe x1 slot is available
appliesWhen: an external drive uses the external version of SATA and the PC lacks that port
explanation: eSATA is the external form of SATA. Few boards have the port, so an eSATA adapter card in a PCIe slot adds it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

need: install a new high-end graphics card
clues: the card's edge connector has 16 lanes
the card needs the fastest slot that links straight to the processor
the board also has two short x1 slots free
appliesWhen: a full-length, 16-lane card such as a graphics card is installed
explanation: Graphics cards are usually PCIe x16 cards, and an x16 card fits only an x16 slot. The x16 slots connect directly to the CPU.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

need: add an NVMe SSD to a small PC with no drive bays
clues: the drive is a small gumstick-shaped circuit board
the case has no room for drive cables
the drive must get its power and data from the board itself
appliesWhen: a small card-style drive connects straight to the board with no cables
explanation: M.2 slots hold M.2 SSDs, including NVMe drives, right on the board. The drive gets power and data from the slot, so no cables are needed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

need: connect a second 2.5-inch SSD inside a desktop
clues: the drive has a 7-pin data socket
the drive is not an NVMe module and has no edge connector
a cable must run from the drive to the board
appliesWhen: an internal 2.5- or 3.5-inch drive connects with a 7-pin data cable
explanation: Internal hard drives, SSDs, and optical drives use 7-pin SATA data cables. The board has several SATA ports for them.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

need: reuse an old 32-bit parallel interface card in a new PC
clues: the card is a specialized lab controller from about 2008
the card's edge connector does not match any lane-based slot
the vendor does not make a newer version of the card
appliesWhen: an old 32-bit parallel card must be installed
explanation: PCI is the older parallel bus that PCIe replaced. Its cards fit only PCI slots, which few new boards still have.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

need: make the case's front USB ports work after a build
clues: the front USB ports have a cable that ends in a multi-pin plug inside the case
the cable must connect to pins on the board itself
the rear USB ports already work
appliesWhen: front-panel USB ports need a connection to pins on the board
explanation: Front-panel USB ports connect to internal USB headers on the board. Headers are rows of pins for case ports, buttons, LEDs, and fans.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

need: cool an overclocked high-end processor as well as possible
clues: the processor runs at full load for hours during renders
air coolers still let the processor reach its heat limit
the user accepts checking tubes and coolant now and then
appliesWhen: the CPU makes more heat than air cooling can remove
explanation: Liquid cooling moves heat to a radiator with a pump and coolant, and it removes heat the most efficiently of all PC cooling methods. It suits hot, overclocked CPUs, but it can leak and needs some maintenance.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

need: cool a low-power chip in a silent media PC
clues: the chip is rated at about 10 W
the case has no fan mounts
there is room above the chip for a finned metal block
appliesWhen: a low-heat chip can be cooled with no moving parts
explanation: A heat sink conducts heat away from a chip through its metal fins. A passive heat sink has no fan, so it is silent and suits chips that make little heat, such as a chipset.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

need: get hot air out of a case that runs warm
clues: the only fan moving air out of the case is the one in the power supply
the CPU and GPU coolers work normally
a mounting spot with four screw holes at the back of the chassis is empty
appliesWhen: warm air builds up inside the case because too little air leaves it
explanation: Powerful systems need at least one exhaust fan at the back, and often a front intake fan. Air should come in at the front and leave at the back or top.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

need: fit a new stock cooler that has a pre-applied layer on its base
clues: the cooler came in the box with the processor
the CPU's top surface is clean and bare
the user has no tube of compound at hand

answer.item: The factory-applied thermal pad on the cooler

appliesWhen: a new cooler already has its own thermal material applied
explanation: Thermal material fills the tiny gaps between the CPU and the heat sink. Many new coolers come with a factory-applied pad or compound, so a first install needs nothing more; a reinstall needs fresh paste.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

clues: the CPU gets very hot within minutes of starting
the overheating began after the cooler was taken off to clean it
the processor overheats even though the cooler is firmly locked down and its fan spins at normal speed
a dry and cracked gray layer is seen on the overheating processor once its cooler is lifted

answer.cause: old or missing thermal paste between the CPU and the heat sink
answer.action: Clean off the old paste with isopropyl alcohol and apply fresh thermal paste

firstStep: Check the CPU temperature and fan speed in the BIOS/UEFI
appliesWhen: the cooler was removed and refitted without fresh paste
explanation: Thermal paste fills the small gaps between the CPU cap and the heat sink. Each time a heat sink is removed, the old paste must be cleaned off and new paste applied.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

clues: the PC shuts down a few minutes after each start
the hardware monitor shows the CPU overheating with 0 RPM for its cooler
the PC that keeps shutting down has its cooler's small 4-pin lead hanging loose next to the socket
the PC still shuts itself down even though the case fans and the power supply fan spin normally

answer.cause: a CPU fan that is not plugged into its motherboard header
answer.action: Connect the CPU fan's lead to the CPU_FAN header

firstStep: Check the CPU fan speed in the BIOS/UEFI hardware monitor
appliesWhen: the processor cooler's fan has no power from the board
explanation: The CPU fan gets power from the CPU fan header on the board. When it is not connected, the CPU overheats and the system shuts down to protect itself.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

clues: the radiator fans spin but the CPU still overheats
the tube at the overheating CPU's block is hot while the radiator stays cool
the gentle hum from the CPU block stopped around the time the overheating began
the processor under a five-year-old closed-loop cooler now reaches its heat limit within minutes

answer.cause: a failed pump in the liquid cooling system
answer.action: Replace the closed-loop liquid cooler

appliesWhen: the coolant no longer moves between the CPU block and the radiator
explanation: A liquid cooler relies on its pump to carry hot coolant to the radiator. Pumps can fail over time, and then the radiator fans cannot remove the CPU's heat.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

clues: the PC reboots at random under load
the CPU runs hot under load and its cooler wobbles when touched
the PC overheats under load with one plastic push-pin anchor of the cooler not locked
the random reboots began after a technician moved the PC to another desk last week

answer.cause: a heat sink that is not seated flush on the CPU
answer.action: Reseat the heat sink with fresh paste and lock every anchor

appliesWhen: the heat sink has come loose and no longer sits flat on the CPU
explanation: A loose heat sink cannot draw heat away from the CPU, which can cause overheating and random reboots. It must sit flush, with every anchor locked.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

clues: the BIOS/UEFI shows only one fan where the case has five
changing the fan profile speeds up all case fans together or not at all
the case fans cannot be controlled one by one even though four of the board's five fan headers are empty

answer.cause: case fans connected through a fan hub instead of separate board headers
answer.action: Connect each case fan to its own motherboard fan header

appliesWhen: the board cannot see or control each fan because the fans share one hub
explanation: The board controls only fans plugged into its fan headers. A fan hub shows all its fans as one, so their speeds cannot be set one by one.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

clues: the new processor will not sit flat in the socket
the contacts do not match even when the pin 1 marks on the processor and the socket line up
the processor that will not seat is from a different maker than the board's chipset

answer.cause: a CPU made for a different socket than the motherboard has
answer.action: Exchange the CPU for one on the motherboard's CPU support list

appliesWhen: the CPU and the board use different socket types
explanation: Intel and AMD CPUs use different sockets, and each socket accepts only its own CPUs. Check the board's CPU support list for the socket and the chipset before buying.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

clues: the PC shows no image even though the new processor fits the socket
the PC has shown no image since the processor upgrade though its fans spin
the processor that gives no image is a newer generation than the board was sold with
the PC starts normally when the old processor is put back in the same board

answer.cause: motherboard firmware that is too old to support the new CPU
answer.action: Flash the BIOS/UEFI to a version that supports the new CPU

appliesWhen: a newer CPU fits the socket but the board's firmware does not know it
explanation: A CPU can share a socket with older models and still need newer firmware. Check the board's support list and update the BIOS/UEFI before or during the upgrade.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

clues: the PC shows a black screen with a blinking cursor at the top left
a flash drive that holds only photos sat in a USB port when the PC failed to start
the PC fails to start Windows only on days when something is plugged into it
the operating system sometimes does not load even though the system drive passes the maker's diagnostic test

answer.cause: a boot order that tries USB devices before the system drive
answer.action: Set the system drive first in the boot options

firstStep: Remove the flash drive and restart the PC
appliesWhen: the firmware tries a removable device before the drive that has the OS
explanation: The boot order decides which device the firmware tries first. When USB is first, an inserted flash drive stops the OS from loading, so the system drive should be first.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

clues: the screen has stayed black since a new video card was installed today
the monitor shows a no-signal message while the new card's fans spin
the monitor that stays black is plugged into the port above the rear USB ports
the picture was fine before the upgrade, when the monitor used the same rear port

answer.cause: a monitor cable plugged into the board's own video port instead of the card
answer.action: Plug the monitor cable into a port on the video card

appliesWhen: the display is connected to the integrated video port while a video card is in use
explanation: When a video card is installed, most boards turn off their built-in video. The monitor must be connected to a port on the card.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies

clues: the case button has done nothing since the motherboard was replaced
the PC will not turn on from the case button though a light on the board shows standby power
the PC that ignores its case button starts when two pins on the board's edge are briefly touched
the case button has not worked since the thin 2-pin plugs from the case were connected to the new board without the manual

answer.cause: the case's power switch lead on the wrong front panel header pins
answer.action: Connect the POWER SW lead to the pins shown in the motherboard manual

appliesWhen: the case button's lead is not on its own header pins
explanation: The front panel header connects the case's power and reset buttons and LEDs to the board. Each lead must go on the pins named in the manual, and the LEDs must also be the right way round.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

clues: the clock shows a date years in the past at each start
the boot order goes back to defaults whenever the PC is unplugged
the eight-year-old PC shows a checksum error message at startup

answer.cause: a dead CMOS battery
answer.action: Replace the CR2032 battery on the motherboard

firstStep: Check the date and time in the BIOS/UEFI setup
appliesWhen: the PC loses its firmware settings and time whenever it is unplugged
explanation: The firmware settings and the clock are kept by a small lithium battery on the board. When it dies, the date and settings reset each time the PC loses power.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

need: keep a file server running if its power supply fails
clues: the server holds the shared files for the whole company
a failed supply must be swapped without shutting the server down
each supply can plug into a different power circuit
appliesWhen: the system must keep running when one supply fails
explanation: A redundant setup has two or more power supplies, each with its own cord, all running at once. If one fails, the other carries the load with no downtime, and many units are hot-swappable.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

need: build a tidy small PC with good airflow
clues: loose spare cables blocked the airflow in the last build
the builder wants to attach only the leads the parts need
more leads may be added later for new drives
appliesWhen: only the cables the build needs should be attached
explanation: A modular power supply has detachable cables, so only the needed leads are connected. That keeps the case tidy and helps airflow.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

need: lower the power bill of PCs that run all day
clues: the PCs work at a moderate load most of the time
the owner wants less power lost as heat
the budget allows a little more now for savings later
appliesWhen: less power should be lost when the supply changes AC to DC
explanation: A power supply loses some power as heat when it turns AC into DC. The 80 Plus rating means at least 80 percent is converted, and higher levels such as Gold waste less.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

need: add a second graphics card to a workstation
clues: the parts list adds up to 780 W at full load
the current 500 W unit already runs near its limit
the user plans to add more drives next year

answer.item: A power supply with a higher wattage rating

appliesWhen: the parts need more power than the current supply can give
explanation: The wattage rating is the most power a supply can give at full load. Add up what all the parts need, then choose a supply above that total with room for growth.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

need: ship the same PC model to offices in the United States and Europe
clues: some offices have 120 VAC outlets and others 230 VAC
users must not have to set any switch on the back
the label must list the whole input range

answer.item: An auto-switching power supply rated 100–240 VAC

appliesWhen: the PC must work on both 110–120 VAC and 220–240 VAC with no switch
explanation: The United States supplies 110–120 VAC, and Europe 220–240 VAC. A universal-input supply detects the voltage, so the same PC works on both without setting a switch.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

need: power a new 2.5-inch SSD
clues: the drive has a flat 15-pin power socket
the drive can use 3.3 V, 5 V, and 12 V
the drive's 7-pin data cable is already connected
appliesWhen: a modern internal drive needs power through a flat 15-pin socket
explanation: SATA power connectors have 15 pins and carry 3.3 V, 5 V, and 12 V. They power SATA hard drives, SSDs, and optical drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies

need: power an old IDE drive moved into a newer PC
clues: the drive has a thick 4-pin power socket
the drive needs only 5 V and 12 V
the drive is too old to have a flat power socket
appliesWhen: an older drive or fan has a thick 4-pin power socket
explanation: The Molex connector is a thick 4-pin plug that carries 5 V and 12 V. Older PATA drives and some fans use it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

need: power a graphics card that draws more than its slot can supply
clues: the card has an 8-pin power socket on its edge
the card's manual lists about 200 W of total board power
the socket is meant for the graphics card rather than the processor
appliesWhen: an expansion card needs extra 12 V power beyond what its slot gives
explanation: PCIe slots give up to 75 W, so stronger graphics cards need 6-pin or 8-pin PCIe power leads. The 6+2-pin plug fits either socket.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

need: give the processor its own 12 V supply on a new board
clues: the board has an 8-pin socket near the CPU socket
the supply has several 8-pin leads with different labels
the board does not POST with only the main lead connected
appliesWhen: the board has an extra 4- or 8-pin socket that feeds the CPU
explanation: Most boards have a 4-pin or 8-pin 12 V socket for the CPU, called EATX12V, as well as the main connector. Do not confuse it with the 8-pin PCIe lead; check the label.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

need: connect a new power supply to an older board with a 20-pin main socket
clues: no adapter cable came with the supply
the new supply's main plug is 24 pins and slightly too long
four pins on the end of the plug can slide off

answer.item: The 20+4-pin main connector with its 4-pin section detached

appliesWhen: a 24-pin supply must fit a board with the older 20-pin main socket
explanation: ATX12V 2.x boards use a 24-pin main connector, while the original ATX boards used 20 pins. Many supplies have a 20+4-pin plug whose extra 4 pins detach for the older boards.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

clues: the PC restarts as soon as a 3D game starts
the restarts began after a high-end graphics card was added last week
the PC runs office programs fine but restarts under heavy graphics load
the PC that restarts in games has a supply whose label shows 400 W

answer.cause: a power supply whose wattage is too low for the new card
answer.action: Replace the power supply with one rated for the full load plus headroom

appliesWhen: the parts draw more power at full load than the supply can give
explanation: A supply with too little wattage can cause brownouts, random reboots, or a PC that will not start. Adding a strong graphics card often pushes the load past the old supply's rating.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

clues: the PC died at its first power-on after it was shipped from a US office to one in Germany
there was a pop and a burnt smell at the first power-on
the PC will no longer start though no one ever touched the red switch on the back of the supply

answer.cause: a voltage selector set to 115 VAC on a 230 VAC outlet
answer.action: Replace the power supply and set the new unit's switch to 230 VAC

appliesWhen: a supply set for 115 VAC was plugged into a 230 VAC outlet
explanation: US outlets give 110–120 VAC and European outlets 220–240 VAC. A dual-voltage supply set to 115 VAC gets about double its voltage on a 230 VAC outlet and is likely damaged.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

clues: the PC has not started since it was moved from a European office to one in the United States
the fans twitch briefly but the PC does not start
the PC will not power on with the red switch on the back of the supply in the European setting

answer.cause: a voltage selector set to 230 VAC on a 115 VAC outlet
answer.action: Power off, unplug, and set the voltage switch to 115 VAC

firstStep: Check the voltage selector switch on the back of the power supply
appliesWhen: a supply set for 230 VAC gets only 110–120 VAC from the outlet
explanation: A supply set to 230 VAC gets only half its expected input from a US outlet, so it cannot power the PC. Unplug it before you change the switch.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

clues: the fans spin but there is no POST since the motherboard was replaced
the main 24-pin lead is firmly in place yet the PC will not POST
only the large main lead and the drive leads were connected before the failed first start

answer.cause: the 8-pin CPU (EATX12V) power lead not connected
answer.action: Connect the 8-pin CPU power lead from the power supply

appliesWhen: the board gets main power but the processor's 12 V socket is empty
explanation: The CPU gets its own 12 V feed through the 4- or 8-pin EATX12V socket. Without it the fans can spin, but the CPU cannot run.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

clues: the new graphics card's fans do not spin
no image comes from any of the card's ports
the new card shows no sign of life while the old card had no sockets on its edge and took all its power from the slot
the PC works when the old low-power card is put back

answer.cause: the PCIe power lead not connected to the graphics card
answer.action: Connect a 6+2-pin PCIe power lead from the power supply to the card

appliesWhen: a graphics card that needs extra 12 V power has no PCIe power lead
explanation: A PCIe slot gives up to 75 W, so stronger cards need 6-pin or 8-pin PCIe power leads. Without them the card does not start.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

need: choose where to put a new department printer
clues: the printer has a wired network port and no Wi-Fi radio
staff from every desk will walk to it to collect pages
only some of the wall jacks in the office are patched to the switch

answer.item: A central spot near a working RJ45 wall jack

appliesWhen: a wired network printer must reach a live network port and be easy for users to get to
explanation: A printer that joins the network by cable must sit near a working RJ45 jack. A central spot also makes it easy for the users to reach.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: choose where to put a new wireless printer
clues: the printer has no wired network port
the chosen corner has no network wall ports
no one has measured the signal strength in that part of the building

answer.item: A spot well inside the Wi-Fi coverage, confirmed with a site survey

appliesWhen: a printer will connect over Wi-Fi and the signal at the planned spot is unknown
explanation: A wireless printer needs a strong signal where it sits. A wireless site survey shows whether the planned spot is well inside the Wi-Fi area, close to an access point.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: choose where to put a printer that one desktop will share
clues: the printer connects only by a USB cable
the team sits together in one area of the office
the host desktop stays on during work hours

answer.item: A shared area next to the PC it will connect to

appliesWhen: a USB printer is shared from one PC, so it must sit beside that PC in a common area
explanation: A USB printer that a PC shares must be close to that PC. A community area next to it lets the other users collect their printouts.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: choose where to put a large new laser printer
clues: the printer gives off a lot of heat while it runs
the user wants to tuck it into a closed cabinet under the desk
the printer's corona wires produce ozone

answer.item: A well-ventilated open area with space around it

appliesWhen: a printer gives off heat or ozone and must not be closed in
explanation: Laser printers make heat and some ozone, so they need good airflow. A closed cubbyhole lets heat build up and shortens the printer's life.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: install a driver for a new general office printer
clues: users print everyday letters, spreadsheets, and reports
no one prints professional graphics on this printer
the office wants the most widely used driver type for general documents
appliesWhen: the printer is for typical office documents such as letters and spreadsheets
explanation: PCL is the more common driver type and is meant for general office printing. It handles letters, spreadsheets, and reports well.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: install a driver for the marketing team's printer
clues: the marketing team prints professional graphics and presentations
the same files must print the same on every printer brand the team uses
fonts and shapes must print exactly as they look on screen
appliesWhen: the users print professional graphics and complex page layouts
explanation: PostScript describes the page with draw and position commands and is the driver type for professional graphics and presentations. It suits high-end printers that print complex layouts.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: set up printing on the new computers
clues: the computers run Windows 11
the printer supports Microsoft's modern print platform
the company wants to stop installing third-party printer drivers

answer.item: The Windows IPP inbox class driver

appliesWhen: Windows 11 computers print to a printer that supports the modern print platform without a vendor driver
explanation: Windows 11 pushes the IPP inbox class driver, part of Microsoft's modern print platform. When the printer supports it, no third-party driver needs to be installed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

need: let new staff print to the existing network printer
clues: the new staff use Mac computers
only Windows drivers are loaded on the print server
the Windows users already print without problems

answer.item: The macOS version of the printer driver

appliesWhen: clients of another operating system need their own driver for the same printer
explanation: A driver must be written for both the printer and the operating system. A print server needs a driver for every type of client that connects, so the Macs need the macOS driver.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: connect a small printer at a home office desk
clues: only one computer will ever print to it
the printer sits right next to the computer
the user does not want the printer on the network

answer.item: A USB cable to the computer

appliesWhen: one computer prints to a local printer that sits next to it
explanation: USB is the most common local printer connection. It is simple, fast, and the computer finds the printer by itself.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: connect the new department printer to the network
clues: the printer must have the most stable connection possible
there is a free RJ45 port in the wall behind it
twenty users will print to it all day
appliesWhen: a shared printer needs the most stable network link and a wall port is close by
explanation: A hardwired connection is the most stable way to put a printer on the network. The printer's built-in NIC lets every user send jobs to it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: connect a printer that sits on a rolling cart
clues: every room it visits is covered by the office access points
no network cable can reach the places where it stops
it must stay connected to the office network all the time

answer.item: The office Wi-Fi network in infrastructure mode

appliesWhen: a printer must stay on the network without a cable
explanation: Joining the existing Wi-Fi network in infrastructure mode keeps the printer on the network wherever the signal reaches. A cable or a short-range link would not follow the cart.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: let a sales rep print from a phone to a small portable printer
clues: the phone and the printer are within a few meters of each other
there is no network at the trade show booth
the link is needed only for a short time
appliesWhen: a phone prints to a nearby portable printer for a short time with no network
explanation: Bluetooth is a short-range link of about 10 meters that pairs a phone with a printer directly. It needs no network and suits a temporary connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: let three coworkers print to a USB printer on the manager's desktop
clues: the printer has no network port
the manager's desktop stays on during work hours
the office has no server

answer.item: Turn on file and printer sharing and share the printer from that PC

appliesWhen: a USB printer on one PC must be used by a few others and that PC is always on
explanation: A printer attached to a Windows PC must be shared before other computers can print to it. Turn on file and printer sharing, then share the printer on its Sharing tab.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: manage printing for 60 printers in the building
clues: permissions must be set for each group on each printer
clients on Windows, macOS, and Linux must get their drivers from one place
printing must not depend on a user's desktop being on
appliesWhen: many printers need central control, permissions, and drivers for every client type
explanation: A print server hosts the printers, processes the jobs, and gives granular control over permissions. It holds the drivers for every client type that connects.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: spread a heavy print load across three identical printers
clues: the three printers sit side by side in one copy room
users should see one printer name
jobs pile up on one printer while the others stand idle

answer.item: Printer pooling on the Ports tab

appliesWhen: several identical printers in one place should share the jobs under one name
explanation: Printer pooling links several physical printers to one printer name, and a job prints on any free device. All the pooled printers must be in the same place so users find their pages.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: print a report on a printer in a branch office in another city
clues: the user is not on the branch office network
the company already pays for an online print service
no VPN is set up between the offices
appliesWhen: a user must print to a printer in a remote office through an online service
explanation: Cloud-based printing lets a user print to a printer in another city by selecting it from a list. It does not need a direct connection to that office's network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

need: add a network printer that Windows did not find on its own
clues: the printer's panel shows a fixed 192.168.1.40, in the same subnet as the PCs
the printer's web page opens when its address is typed in a browser
the printer is plugged straight into the network switch

answer.item: Add the printer with a TCP/IP address or hostname

appliesWhen: a network printer has a known IP address but is not found automatically
explanation: A network-aware printer is a host with its own IP address. Adding it by that address sends jobs straight to the printer, so no PC has to act as the print server.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: cut the department's paper use in half
clues: most jobs are long reports
the reports are read once and then filed
each sheet comes out with text on only one face
appliesWhen: pages must be printed on both sides of the sheet
explanation: Duplexing prints on both sides of the paper, which halves the sheets a long report uses. Most printers are not set to duplex by default.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: print a wide spreadsheet so that every column fits on the page
clues: the right-hand columns are cut off
the sheet is much wider than it is tall
shrinking the text makes it too small to read
appliesWhen: the content is wider than it is tall, such as a spreadsheet or slides
explanation: Orientation sets whether the page is printed vertically or horizontally. A wide spreadsheet fits best when the page is turned sideways.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: print contracts on legal-size paper
clues: the legal sheets are loaded in the second drawer
jobs keep coming out on letter paper from the first drawer
the drawer guides are already set for the longer sheets
appliesWhen: a job must come from a particular drawer that holds another paper size
explanation: Tray settings choose which drawer, and which paper size, a job uses. In Windows they are in Printing preferences, often in the Advanced section.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: print a brochure with detailed photos for customers
clues: fine details in the photos look rough
the printer is set to its normal mode
speed matters less than how the brochure looks
appliesWhen: output with graphics must show more detail
explanation: Quality is the print resolution in dots per inch. 600 DPI is letter quality, but 1200 or 2400 DPI shows graphics with more detail.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: print 30 copies of a 10-page handout
clues: the last job came out as all the page 1s, then all the page 2s
staff spent an hour sorting pages by hand
each copy must be a complete set in page order
appliesWhen: several copies of a multipage job must each come out as a complete ordered set
explanation: Collating prints page 1, 2, 3 of one copy and then starts the next copy. It saves the users from sorting the pages by hand.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: make sure only staff can use the lobby multifunction printer
clues: visitors have been making copies on it
staff do not carry ID cards
the device can check network account credentials
appliesWhen: users must prove who they are with credentials before they use the device
explanation: User authentication makes each person sign in before the device copies, scans, or prints. Without valid credentials a visitor cannot use it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: let staff sign in to the multifunction printer quickly
clues: users find typing a password on the touchscreen slow
every employee carries a company ID card
the device has a slot on its side for scanning cards
appliesWhen: staff carry ID cards and should sign in to the device by scanning them
explanation: Badging signs a user in when they scan their work badge at the device's reader. It is faster than typing a username and password and still identifies the user.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: keep HR printouts from sitting in the output tray
clues: the human resources team prints confidential personnel files
the printer is in a busy shared hallway
staff want the job to start only when they are standing at the device

answer.item: Secured prints that hold each job until the user releases it

appliesWhen: a confidential job must wait at the printer until its owner is there
explanation: A secured prints feature holds the job until the user authenticates at the printer and starts it. Confidential pages are never left in the tray.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: find out who printed a leaked document last week
clues: the document was printed on a shared printer
dozens of staff use the printer every day
the event is already in the past
appliesWhen: someone must find out after the fact who printed what, where, and when
explanation: Audit logs record who printed which document, when, and where. Auditing usually has to be enabled before the event, on the printer or in Windows.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: send a signed two-page form to a customer at once
clues: the customer is outside the company
the file will be small
the customer has no access to the company's file shares
appliesWhen: a small scan must go straight to a person's inbox
explanation: Scan to email sends the scanned file, usually as a PDF, to a recipient. It is the most common way to send a scan to someone.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: store scanned invoices on the company file server
clues: the scans are often too large for the mail server
the accounting team opens them from a share on a Windows server
the files must stay inside the company network

answer.item: Scan to a network folder over SMB

appliesWhen: scans must be saved to a shared folder on a server, often because they are too large for email
explanation: Scan to folder saves the file in a shared network folder using the Server Message Block protocol. The device must be set up for SMB scanning and the share must be secured.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: save scanned drawings where remote staff can open them
clues: the staff work from home and on the road
the company keeps its files in OneDrive
there is no VPN to the office
appliesWhen: scans must go to an online storage service that remote users reach
explanation: Scan to cloud saves the file in a service such as OneDrive, Google Drive, or Dropbox. Remote users open it there without a link to the office network.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: scan a 40-page contract into one file
clues: the pages are loose and unstapled
placing each page on the glass would take too long
the pages are all the same letter size
appliesWhen: many loose pages must be scanned in one job
explanation: An ADF pulls a stack of loose pages through the scanner one at a time, often up to 50 pages in one job. No one has to place each page on the glass.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: scan two pages from a bound book
clues: the book cannot be taken apart
the item is too thick to go through the feed rollers
the pages must lie flat to scan cleanly
appliesWhen: a bound, thick, or fragile item must be laid on the glass
explanation: A flatbed scanner scans one item laid face down on the glass under the lid. It handles books and fragile items that cannot be fed through rollers.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: pages have come out blank since the printer was unboxed and set up today
every page comes out completely blank
nothing appears on the pages even though the display shows the supply as full
a test page from the control panel is also blank

answer.cause: the protective strip still on the new toner cartridge
answer.action: Remove the cartridge and pull off its protective strip

appliesWhen: a new printer or cartridge still has its shipping tape in place
explanation: Toner cartridges ship with a protective strip that keeps the toner in. If it is not removed the printer cannot print, and it can even be damaged.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: pages fill with strange symbols and lines of code
a one-page document prints many pages
jobs from the PC print garbage while a test page from the printer's own panel prints correctly
the garbled pages began after the printer was added on the PC with a generic model name

answer.cause: the wrong printer driver on the PC
answer.action: Install the correct driver for the printer model and operating system

firstStep: Print a test page from the printer's control panel
appliesWhen: the PC sends the job in a page language the printer does not use
explanation: With the wrong driver the PC sends commands in the wrong page-description language. The printer prints those commands as text, often over many pages.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: a security bulletin lists the printer model as vulnerable
the mobile printing option in the new manual is missing from the menus
the printer lacks features that the current manual lists and has run the same embedded software since it was bought

answer.cause: outdated printer firmware
answer.action: Download the latest firmware from the manufacturer's website and install it

appliesWhen: the printer's embedded software is old and lacks fixes or features
explanation: Firmware is the printer's embedded software, like a motherboard's BIOS. Updates add features such as mobile printing and fix bugs and security holes.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: coworkers cannot print early in the morning
printing works again once the owner arrives
the printer that coworkers cannot reach in the morning is connected by USB to a coworker's desktop
jobs from coworkers fail even though the printer itself is on and ready

answer.cause: the PC that shares the printer is turned off

only printing fails while other network devices work normally

explanation: A TCP/IP printer needs an IP address on the same subnet as the computers that add it. With an address from another subnet the jobs cannot reach it.

the Macs on the first floor where the printer sits find it at once
the second-floor Macs that cannot find the printer reach the internet and the file server normally
the second-floor Macs cannot discover the printer even though it prints for anyone who has already added it by address

answer.cause: the printer is on the other side of a router from the Macs
answer.action: Add the printer by its IP address instead of waiting for discovery

appliesWhen: automatic discovery fails because the printer is in another broadcast domain
explanation: Bonjour finds devices only within one broadcast domain. It does not see a printer on the other side of a router, so the printer must be added by its address.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: users cannot find their printouts
jobs sent to one printer name come out on any of several devices
some lost printouts turn up on two devices on another floor

answer.cause: a printer pool that includes printers in different rooms
answer.action: Keep only printers that sit in the same room in the pool

appliesWhen: pooled printers are spread out, so jobs come out far away
explanation: Printer pooling sends a job to any printer in the pool. When the pooled printers are in different places, users walk around looking for their pages.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: the printer asks for letter paper though legal sheets are loaded in drawer 2

answer.cause: the tray paper size setting does not match the loaded paper
answer.action: Set the drawer's paper size in the printer settings to match the paper

appliesWhen: the configured paper size for a drawer differs from the paper in it
explanation: Tray settings tell the printer what paper size each drawer holds. When the setting and the paper differ, the printer stops and asks for the paper it expects.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: scans to the file server fail with an access denied error

answer.action: Give the scanner's account write permission on the share

appliesWhen: the destination share or its permissions do not let the device save files
explanation: Scan to folder uses SMB, and the destination share must be set up and secured for the device. If its account cannot write there, every scan fails with access denied.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

the mail server returns a message that the attachment is too big

answer.cause: the scanned file is larger than the email size limit
answer.action: Scan the large job to a network folder over SMB instead

appliesWhen: a scan is too large to be sent by email
explanation: Mail servers limit the size of a message. A large scan can be saved to a network folder over SMB instead, which has no such limit.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices
