clues: the display shows a service message
the service message appeared on a printer that has printed about 200,000 pages
the printer that shows the service message has paper pickup rollers worn smooth
pages still print normally despite the service message on the display

answer.cause: the page count reached the maintenance interval
answer.action: Install the maintenance kit and reset the page counter

appliesWhen: the printer's page counter reached the service interval
explanation: Laser printers count pages and show a maintenance message at the set interval. The kit replaces worn parts such as the fuser, rollers, and separation pads, and the counter must then be reset.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: print has grown lighter over several days
the display shows a supply warning as the print gets lighter
the fading is even across the whole sheet
print has faded on a printer that has had nothing replaced for a year

answer.cause: a nearly empty toner cartridge
answer.action: Replace the toner cartridge with the model the manufacturer specifies

appliesWhen: the consumable that makes the image on laser pages is running out
explanation: Toner is the laser printer's consumable, and pages fade evenly as it runs out. Use the cartridge model the manufacturer specifies, not a refilled one.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: text sits too close to one edge of the page
lines on the test page print slightly out of place
the misplaced printing began after the rollers and fuser were replaced yesterday
margins on printed pages no longer match the margins set in the document

answer.cause: the printer was not calibrated after maintenance
answer.action: Run the printer's calibration routine

appliesWhen: margins or colors are out of line after parts or supplies were changed
explanation: Calibration sets the horizontal and vertical print positions and the margins so text and images print straight. It should be run after maintenance, from the printer's firmware or from Windows.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

clues: black powder coats the inside of the front cover
gray smudges show on the back of pages
the smudged pages began after a cartridge was dropped while it was being changed

answer.cause: loose toner spilled inside the printer
answer.action: Clean out the printer with a toner vacuum

appliesWhen: loose powder from a cartridge has spread inside the printer
explanation: Spilled toner smears pages and should not be breathed in. A toner vacuum picks it up; compressed air is used only outdoors, and the residue is then vacuumed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers

clues: thin white lines run across the printed photos
the white lines appeared the first time the printer was used after two months
photos print with gaps even though the ink levels show plenty left
a test pattern has missing bars

answer.cause: clogged printhead nozzles
answer.action: Run the printhead cleaning cycle

appliesWhen: dried ink blocks part of the printhead
explanation: Ink dries in the printhead when the printer sits unused, so some lines do not print. The printer's cleaning routine clears the printhead; a cleaning solution helps when the routine is not enough.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: vertical lines look jagged
colors are slightly offset from the black text
the jagged printing began after the ink supplies were changed this morning

answer.cause: the cartridges were not aligned after they were replaced
answer.action: Run the alignment (calibration) routine

appliesWhen: new cartridges are out of line with each other
explanation: Inkjet printers should be calibrated after cartridges are replaced so lines line up and colors blend. The routine prints a pattern and asks which set looks best.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: the printer stops and will not print anything
the display shows the cyan level at zero and a stop message
the printer will not print even black text though the other colors are still half full

answer.cause: an empty ink cartridge
answer.action: Replace the empty cartridge with a new one from the manufacturer

appliesWhen: one color has run out and the printer stops
explanation: Some inkjet printers stop working when just one cartridge is empty. A new cartridge from the manufacturer fixes it; refill kits can leak and print badly.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: the display reports a jam after nearly every page
the jams began after a stuck sheet was pulled out in pieces last week
the printer clicks while it tries to pull in a sheet and then reports a jam

answer.cause: torn paper caught in the rollers and feeder
answer.action: Open the printer and remove the paper scraps from the rollers and feeder

appliesWhen: bits of paper are left in the paper path
explanation: Bits of a torn sheet left in the roller or feeder block the next page. Inkjet maintenance includes clearing jams and removing any caught paper.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

clues: a faint blank streak runs down every printout
the printouts with the blank streak come from a print head ringed with paper dust
the streak on the printouts has grown over months of all-day use at a busy counter

answer.cause: a dirty heating element
answer.action: Clean the heating element with a thermal printer cleaning pen or card

appliesWhen: dust or residue on the heating element keeps part of the paper from being heated
explanation: Dust and residue on the heating element stop it heating that part of the paper. Unplug the printer, let it cool, and clean the element with a cleaning pen or card.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: printouts come out completely blank
printouts have been blank since the roll was changed a few minutes ago
scratching the outer face of the roll that prints blank leaves no dark mark

answer.cause: the paper roll is loaded upside down
answer.action: Reload the roll with the coated side facing the print head

firstStep: Scratch both sides of the paper with a fingernail to find the coated side
appliesWhen: the coated side of the paper faces away from the head
explanation: Only the coated side of thermal paper darkens with heat. If the roll is loaded the wrong way the head heats the plain side and nothing shows.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: new rolls are already gray before anything prints
the gray rolls all come from a box that sits on a sunny windowsill
printouts are hard to read on the dark background

answer.cause: the spare rolls were stored in heat and sunlight
answer.action: Replace the darkened rolls and store spares in a cool, dark place

appliesWhen: the paper has darkened from heat or sunlight in storage
explanation: Thermal paper turns dark when it gets warm, even before it prints. Spare rolls must be kept away from direct sunlight and heat.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

clues: printouts have come out blank since the rolls began coming from a cheaper supplier
printouts are fine whenever an old roll from the former supplier is loaded
the paper that prints blank does not darken when it is scratched on either side

answer.cause: plain paper instead of heat-sensitive paper
answer.action: Load the special thermal paper made for the printer

appliesWhen: the roll is ordinary paper with no heat-sensitive coating
explanation: Thermal printers print only on special heat-sensitive paper. Ordinary paper has no coating, so the heated head leaves no mark.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: the paper stops moving after a few lines
the printer makes a grinding sound
bits of a torn printout are visible near the rubber roller where the paper stalls

answer.cause: debris blocking the feed assembly
answer.action: Remove the debris from the feed assembly with compressed air or a computer vacuum

appliesWhen: debris in the paper path stops the paper from moving
explanation: The feed assembly moves the paper past the head on a rubber platen roller. Debris there stops the paper; remove it with compressed air or a vacuum after the printer is unplugged and cool.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: print on the invoices is faint and gray
the fading is even across every character
the print has faded on a printer that has had no supplies changed for many months

answer.cause: a worn-out ink ribbon
answer.action: Replace the ribbon with the model the manufacturer specifies

appliesWhen: the inked strip the pins strike has run dry
explanation: An impact printer's pins strike an inked ribbon, which dries out with use. A dry ribbon prints faint, even characters and must be replaced with the manufacturer's model.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: a thin white line runs through every line of text
the gap is at the same height in every character
a new ribbon did not remove the white line through the text

answer.cause: a bent or broken pin in the printhead
answer.action: Replace the printhead with an authorized part

appliesWhen: one pin of the print head no longer strikes the ribbon
explanation: A dot-matrix print head forms characters from a matrix of 9 or 24 pins. When one pin fails, the same row of dots is missing in every character.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

clues: the paper drifts to one side and jams
torn bits of the perforated side strips are inside the printer
the jams began after the box of continuous paper was changed this morning

answer.cause: continuous paper loaded out of line on the tractor feed
answer.action: Clear out the torn strips and reload the paper straight on the tractor pins

appliesWhen: the continuous paper is not lined up on the feed pins
explanation: Impact printers pull continuous paper by the holes on its sides. Paper loaded out of line feeds crookedly and jams, and torn strips must be cleared out.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: print invoices that make copies for the customer and the shop
clues: each invoice form has three layered sheets
the copies underneath are marked only by force on the top sheet
the forms come as continuous paper with holes along the sides
appliesWhen: multipart forms need a physical strike to mark every copy
explanation: Multipart paper makes copies only when force is applied to the top sheet. Impact printers strike the paper through a ribbon; laser, inkjet, and thermal printers do not.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: print receipts at each checkout lane
clues: the printer must be small and quiet
no ink, toner, or ribbon should ever need changing
receipts come off a narrow roll
appliesWhen: receipts print on a roll at a point-of-sale station with no ink to change
explanation: Thermal printers heat special coated paper to make the image, so they use no ink, toner, or ribbon. They are the usual printer for point-of-sale receipts.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

need: print hundreds of text pages a day for the whole office
clues: the printer must print 40 or more pages per minute
the text must be crisp at letter quality
the cost per page must stay low at high volume
appliesWhen: an office needs fast, high-volume printing on cut sheets
explanation: Laser printers print 10 to 100 pages per minute at 600 DPI or more. They are the most common business printer for high volumes of documents.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

need: print color photos in a small home office
clues: the user prints only a few pages a week
the budget for the printer itself is small
photo prints matter more than speed
appliesWhen: a home user prints a few color photos and graphics
explanation: Inkjet printers are common in home offices and mostly print color photos and graphics. They are cheap to buy and simple to maintain.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance
